records.name: Prepared Place Ministries
records.summary: A nonprofit that trains and supports women affected by incarceration, both inside and outside prison. It also serves their families and works with churches and local service providers.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as a transitional coach or in another Chill Out role, donate, or request a speaker. The site describes the Chill Out mentorship program but does not say how to enroll.

cost.text: No program fee listed; the site asks for donations

first_step.how: Fill out the online volunteer form on the Volunteer page and pick a Zoom orientation; someone from the ministry then contacts you.
first_step.basis: The way in is a web form and a Zoom orientation, but the orientation dates have no year and the site footers read 2016, so the next step is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The volunteer role described is sharing faith with people behind prison walls and supporting prisoners, their families and their communities. Orientation for transitional coaches is held on Zoom, and the site does not say how long it runs or what it covers.
first_visit_tips: The group lists a mailing address, a phone line and a contact form, but no office hours, so call or write before you plan anything.
The orientation dates on the volunteer page have no year, so confirm the next date before you plan around it.
Chill Out Church services meet every 5th Sunday inside the Philadelphia Industrial Correctional Center, and the page invites churches and groups to contact the ministry to take part.

records.notes: Footers on the contact, Chill Out and Chill Out Church pages read 2016, and the volunteer page's orientation dates (April 12 and 19) have no year. No item dated in the last 24 months was found, so status stays probably_active under the working-site rule, but treat it as stale until a phone call confirms it. The newsletter sign-up mentioned on the homepage was not found on the contact page, so it was removed from what_you_do. The faith-community category was added because Chill Out is a faith-based program. The one WebSearch returned only directory profiles that disagree on the address (P.O. Box 2120 versus an Elmwood Avenue address) and name a second domain (preparedplacemin.org); none of that is recorded. Fetches used: 5.

records.name: Presbyterian Church of Chestnut Hill
records.summary: A Presbyterian church on Germantown Avenue with Sunday worship, children and youth programs, a Wednesday Bible study, and music events.
records.what_you_do: Join Sunday worship at 10 am, the Wednesday morning Bible study, a weekend of service, or one of the music events on the calendar.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 10 am, with Church School at 10:20 and fellowship at 11:15. Bible study on Wednesday mornings at 10:30 am, and a Thursday evening faith conversation called Theology on Tap.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10 am at 8855 Germantown Avenue, or call 215-247-8855 or email info@chestnuthillpres.org first to ask about visiting.
first_step.basis: A Warm Welcome page says all are welcome and invites people to visit, with a phone line, an email address and a contact page for questions. There is no newcomer class or first-timer event, so it does not reach a 5.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Sunday visit starts with worship at 10 am, with scripture, preaching and music. Children through grade 5 leave for church school before the sermon, while youth and adults stay in worship. Coffee and fellowship follow around 11:15, and an adult education hour called Second Hour runs at 11:30. The site does not say how long the service lasts or what to wear.
first_visit_tips: Children through grade 5 go to church school before the sermon; sixth graders can choose church school or staying in worship.
Coffee is served after worship, and fellowship starts at 11:15.
The weekly bulletin shows the week's service, and a livestream is offered if you want to watch first.

records.notes: Membership runs through an external member portal, which was not checked. The bulletin PDF itself could not be read as text, so the October 4, 2026 bulletin date comes from the worship page. The Wednesday time (10:30 am) comes from the Warm Welcome page; the Wednesday Bible Study link goes to a page with no time. No parking, transit or accessibility details are published, so none are recorded. Concerts and a weekend of service are on the calendar, but their dates have no year, so they do not set the status. Fetches used: 5.

records.name: The River Church
records.summary: A Christian church on Island Avenue in Philadelphia with Sunday worship, a Thursday night midweek service, and programs for children, youth, singles, and the arts.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship at 10 am or to Midweek Manna, a prayer and Bible study on Thursday at 7 pm. Children and youth go to their own classes during the Sunday message. The site names leaders for dance, arts, and singles ministries but does not say how to join them.

schedule.text: Sunday morning worship at 10 am, with children's and youth classes during the Sunday message. Midweek Manna prayer and Bible study every Thursday at 7 pm.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 10 am or Thursday Midweek Manna at 7 pm at 3751 Island Avenue, or call 215-873-1230 or send a note through the Contact Us form first.
first_step.basis: The site says its doors are always open and gives clear service times and a phone line, but it does not describe a newcomer welcome or program.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Sunday visit starts with worship at 10 am. Children stay for the first part with their parents, then go to a Bible class during the message, and youth have their own class at the same time. Thursday Midweek Manna is a prayer and Bible study at 7 pm. The site does not say how long the service runs or what to wear.
first_visit_tips: Children join the first part of Sunday worship, then leave for their class during the message.
The site lists no office hours, so call 215-873-1230 or use the Contact Us form to ask about visiting first.
A Get directions link is on the site, but no parking or transit notes are given.

records.notes: Also known as Present Truth Ministries (the aka in the batch). Marriage Conference 2026 is listed with no month, so it does not set last_sign_of_life. The site has no visitor, children or youth pages, so the children and youth details come from the homepage and contact page. Parking, transit and accessibility are not published. The Rivers of Life School of Ministry is named on the site and is listed in leads_only. Fetches used: 3.

records.name: Prisoner Visitation and Support
records.summary: A volunteer group that visits people held in federal and military prisons across the United States, a service it says it has provided since 1968. Trained volunteers visit about once a month, keep up brief correspondence, and write a short report after each visit.
records.what_you_do: Become a volunteer visitor and commit to at least two years of visits, or give money to help recruit and train volunteers.

schedule.text: Visitors see the person they are matched with about once a month, keep up brief correspondence in between, and file a short online report after each visit. Training comes before the first visit.

cost.text: The site does not state a volunteer fee; it asks for donations to recruit and train volunteers.

first_step.how: Download the fillable visitor application from the Become a Visitor page, then talk with PVS staff, complete training and wait for facility approval before your first visit.
first_step.basis: The way in is a written application, a staff conversation, training and facility approval with fingerprinting and a background check, then a match. The group asks for at least two years, so it is not a drop-in group.
first_step.what_to_expect: After approval, you are matched with one person from a waiting list and visit that same person about once a month for at least two years. Visits are face to face inside federal or military prisons; the person sets the agenda, and you listen with respect without preaching. Between visits you send brief correspondence and file a short online report.
first_visit_tips: Expect fingerprinting and a background check before you can visit anyone.
Use the Bureau of Prisons facility locator the group recommends to see whether a federal prison is near you.
Plan for a two year commitment, and tell PVS early if you need to stop so it can notify the prison and the person.

records.notes: The visitor resources page is password protected, so training format, length and the report form could not be read. The become-a-visitor page says training happens but not how long or where. The Friends Center address is the group's office, not a visit site. The visiting-with-us article byline and the become-a-visitor page both show an Oct 2, 2026 date. Fetches used: 4.

records.name: Project Always Receiving
records.summary: A Philadelphia group that works on vacant lots to create shared community space, and runs family events such as a back to school giveaway, a health and wellness fair and open mic nights.
records.what_you_do: Come to the open events, such as the back to school giveaway or the open mic night. Volunteers can use the volunteer form on the group's site.

schedule.text: Community events come up through the year, such as back to school giveaways, health and wellness fairs and open mic nights. The site lists no regular weekly schedule.

locations.label: Boys and Girls Club, Kinsey Street (giveaway venue)

first_step.how: Email Projectalwaysreceiving@gmail.com, or send an inquiry through the general volunteer form on the Volunteers page, to ask about the next event.
first_step.basis: Events are public, and the Volunteers page welcomes volunteers of any background and offers a form and an email. No upcoming events were listed when checked and the last one was in August 2025, so the way in is currently a form or email.
first_step.what_to_expect: Past events ran as afternoon community gatherings, from noon to 3 pm or from noon to 7 pm, with giveaways, a health and wellness fair and an open mic night. Open mic performers signed up through a form. The page does not say whether events cost money or need registration.
first_visit_tips: Check the events page before you go; no upcoming events were listed when we checked.
Open mic performers sign up through a linked form, so plan ahead if you want to perform.
Past venues have street addresses on the site, but no transit or parking details are given.

records.notes: The events page lists three past events in 2025 (May 24, Aug 11 and Aug 30) and no upcoming events. The 2022 founding year and the 2026 copyright footer are not used as evidence of activity. The Volunteers page lists no roles, time commitment or training. Sponsors named on the giveaway page are businesses and are not recorded as partners. Fetches used: 4.

records.name: Project MEOW
records.summary: An all-volunteer cat rescue in West Philadelphia. It traps, neuters and returns community cats, cares for kittens and sick cats, and fosters and adopts out friendly cats.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer, foster a cat or kitten, help a community cat caretaker, or adopt from the adoptable cats listed on the site.

schedule.text: Cat-care shifts run mornings and afternoons or evenings, booked on an online calendar. Colony feeding happens at least once a week between 4 and 7 pm and takes about an hour.

first_step.how: Open the Volunteer page at projectmeow.org and fill out the volunteer application. To foster, use the Foster Form on the fostering page, and a volunteer will get in touch.
first_step.basis: The volunteer application and Foster Form are public and need no dues, and the fostering page says no cat experience is required. The site lists no orientation dates or training steps.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe orientation or a first shift. Roles run from a few hours a week of admin help to a weekly colony feeding near Clark Park that takes about an hour and needs a vehicle. Fostering needs no cat experience, and the site says easy cats are available for beginners.
first_visit_tips: The cat-care shifts at the group's space require being able to lift 20 pounds.
Fosters take kittens to vet visits, and kitten vaccines can mean several trips over two to three months.
Send questions about fostering to fosters@projectmeow.org and general questions to rfa@projectmeow.org.

records.name: Project S.A.V.E.
records.summary: A Philadelphia-area nonprofit that supports people affected by sexual violence, partner violence, and trauma with advocacy, counseling, peer support, and wellness groups.
records.what_you_do: Join a drop-in healing and wellness group, a survivor support group, or a youth program, or call or text the support line to ask about services.

schedule.text: A drop-in Creative Healing and Community Wellness Group meets in the evening, 6 to 7:15 pm, at the Henry Avenue office. Youth programs have run during the day. Support groups run in cycles, so check the events page for the current run.

cost.text: Many services are free for eligible people, with sliding-scale fees for others

first_step.how: Email referrals@projectsavephilly.com with 'Referral Request' in the subject line, or call or text 215-703-8441, and ask about the drop-in Creative Healing and Community Wellness Group or other support.
first_step.basis: The drop-in group and a referral email or call or text line give a clear way in, and education, advocacy and community events do not need eligibility. The site does not describe what a first session or intake looks like, so it does not reach a 4.
first_step.what_to_expect: The drop-in Creative Healing and Community Wellness Group meets in the evening, 6 to 7:15 pm, at the Henry Avenue office, with creative and wellness activities. The page does not say how many people attend, whether you must register, or what it costs. Some direct services have eligibility rules, while education, advocacy, wellness and community events are open to anyone.
first_visit_tips: The suite number differs between pages (227 on the events page, 354 on the contact page), so confirm the room when you call.
Ask about virtual options when you call; the site says some services are offered online depending on staff availability.
Direct services have eligibility rules, so ask which services fit you before you come.

records.notes: The teen age range differs between pages (13 to 17 on the events page, 14 to 18 on the programs page), so no minimum age is set. The Day of Defense on Oct 17, 2026 and Voices Unbroken on Oct 24, 2026 are upcoming events on the events page, which is why last_sign_of_life is October 2026. The virtual Creating a Support Network group (Jul to Sep 2026) and the 10 Year Gathering have passed and are not in schedule text. Beta Zeta Delta Chapter of Zeta Phi Beta co-hosts the Day of Defense and is listed in leads_only. Fetches used: 5.
